findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify the AC: `TicketTransport` is a plain (non-`@runtime_checkable`) Protocol and no construction-time `isinstance` guard exists in the codebase — either scope the @runtime_checkable addition and the construction guard explicitly, or reword the AC to say 'declared on the Protocol and enforced by the structural test' without the isinstance claim, avoiding cargo-culting the capability-Protocol detection pattern onto the required-interface Protocol.
evidence: _backend.py line 80: `class TicketTransport(Protocol):` — no @runtime_checkable decorator, unlike SupportsLinks (line 218), SupportsComments (line 250), SupportsIncremental (line 259), SupportsAbsenceProbe (line 270), and Backend (line 290) which ARE @runtime_checkable
grep of entire rebar_reconciler src: zero hits for `isinstance.*TicketTransport` or `isinstance.*transport`

SupportsLinks et al. are @runtime_checkable because the core dispatches `isinstance(backend, SupportsLinks)` to detect capability — a structurally different role from TicketTransport, which is always-required and never isinstance-detected

The plan's own Testing section correctly names the AST structural test as the guard ('a structural test asserts every transport method the core reconciler calls is declared on the Protocol') — the isinstance claim is redundant and misleading
findings.finding: The plan's AC conflates 'declared on the Protocol' with 'fails an isinstance check at construction' — but TicketTransport is a plain (non-@runtime_checkable) Protocol, and no isinstance(transport, TicketTransport) guard exists anywhere in the construction path. Achieving the runtime isinstance behaviour would require adding @runtime_checkable to TicketTransport AND a new construction-time isinstance assertion in the backend/registry — machinery that doesn't exist today and that risks cargo-culting the @runtime_checkable pattern from SupportsLinks (where isinstance detection is the core dispatch mechanism) onto TicketTransport (where it is not). The structural AST test the plan correctly prescribes is the real guard; the isinstance claim is an overspecification that either goes unimplemented (silently weakening the AC) or introduces unnecessary runtime-Protocol machinery.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — '[ ] the transport surface the core requires is declared on the port, so a transport missing a member fails an isinstance check at construction rather than at runtime mid-pass, asserted by test'
scenarios: Implementer adds @runtime_checkable to TicketTransport and a construction isinstance guard, introducing runtime overhead and a novel Protocol-detection pattern not used elsewhere for required (non-capability) protocols — cargo-culting from capability Protocols.

Implementer treats 'declared on the Protocol' as satisfying the AC without adding any runtime enforcement, leaving the isinstance claim vacuous — the structural test provides the real guard but the AC text misleads future readers about what protection exists.

The plan must name the correct DC path (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/{property_key}`) or explicitly state that `pycontribs/jira`'s library method is used (which handles path versioning internally).

findings.finding: The plan asserts that set_entity_property can be implemented by 'reading Cloud's counterpart first rather than inventing a shape', but does not resolve HOW the DC transport will make the raw REST PUT — pycontribs/jira has no native issue-property method, so raw HTTP is required.
